question: Which one of the following criticisms of the Dickey-Fuller/Engle-Granger approach to dealing with cointegrated variables is overcome by the Engle-Yoo (EY) procedure?
option_a: In the context of small samples, Dickey Fuller tests are prone to conclude that there is a unit root in a series when there is not
option_b: The Engle-Granger (EG) approach can only detect up to one cointegrating relationship even though there could be more than one
option_c: The variables are treated asymmetrically in the cointegrating tests
option_d: It is not possible to perform tests about the cointegrating relationship

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning maximum likelihood (ML) estimation in the context of GARCH models?

i) Maximum likelihood estimation selects the parameter values that maximise the

probability that we would have actually observed the values of the series y that we

actually did.


ii) GARCH models can only be estimated by ML and not by OLS


iii) For estimation of a standard linear model (with no GARCH), the OLS and ML

estimates for the slope and intercept parameters will be identical but the estimator

for the variance of the disturbances is slightly different


iv) Most computer packages use numerical procedures to estimate GARCH models

rather than a set of analytical formulae
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which of the following statements is true concerning forecasting in econometrics?
option_a: Forecasts can only be made for time-series data
option_b: Mis-specified models are certain to produce inaccurate forecasts
option_c: Structural forecasts are simpler to produce than those from time series models
option_d: In-sample forecasting ability is a poor test of model adequacy

question: Consider a series that follows an MA(1) with zero mean and a moving average coefficient of 0.4. What is the value of the autocovariance at lag 1?
option_d: It is not possible to determine the value of the autocovariances without knowing the disturbance variance.

question: If there were a leverage effect in practice, what would be the shape of the news impact curve for as model that accounted for that leverage?
option_a: It would rise more quickly for negative disturbances than for positive ones of the same magnitude
option_b: It would be symmetrical about zero
option_c: It would rise less quickly for negative disturbances than for positive ones of the same magnitude
option_d: It would be zero for all positive disturbances

question: Which of the following statements is false concerning the linear probability model?
option_a: There is nothing in the model to ensure that the estimated probabilities lie between zero and one
option_b: Even if the probabilities are truncated at zero and one, there will probably be many observations for which the probability is either exactly zero or exactly one
option_c: The error terms will be heteroscedastic and not normally distributed
option_d: The model is much harder to estimate than a standard regression model with a continuous dependent variable

question:
Which of the following estimation techniques are available for the estimation of over-identified systems of simultaneous equations?

i) OLS

ii) ILS

iii) 2SLS

iv) IV
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii) and (iv)

question: Suppose that we are interested in testing the null hypothesis that a GARCH(2,2) model can be restricted to a process with a constant conditional variance using the likelihood ratio test approach. Which of the following statements are true?
option_a: The test statistic will follow a chi-squared distribution with 2 degrees of freedom under the null hypothesis
option_b: The value of the log-likelihood function will almost always be bigger for the restricted model than for the unrestricted model
option_c: If the relevant values of the log-likelihood functions are -112.3 and -118.4, the value of the test statistic is 12.2
option_d: The likelihood ratio test compares the slopes of the log-likelihood function at the maximum and at the restricted parameter value.

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the Box-Jenkins approach to diagnostic testing for ARMA models?

(i) The tests will show whether the identified model is either too large or too small

(ii) The tests involve checking the model residuals for autocorrelation, heteroscedasticity, and non-normality

(iii) If the model suggested at the identification stage is appropriate, the acf and pacf for the residuals should show no additional structure

(iv) If the model suggested at the identification stage is appropriate, the coefficients on the additional variables under the overfitting approach will be statistically insignificant
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: A Hausman test would be used for
option_a: Determining whether an equation that is part of a simultaneous system is identified
option_b: Determining whether a simultaneous framework is needed for a particular variable
option_c: Determining whether 2SLS or ILS is optimal
option_d: Determining whether the structural form equations can be obtained via substitution from the reduced forms

question: An ARMA(p,q) (p, q are integers bigger than zero) model will have
option_a: An acf and pacf that both decline geometrically
option_b: An acf that declines geometrically and a pacf that is zero after p lags
option_c: An acf that declines geometrically and a pacf that is zero after q lags
option_d: An acf that is zero after p lags and a pacf that is zero after q lags

(ii) The regressand

(iv) The effect variable

question:
Which of the following could result in autocorrelated residuals?

i) Slowness of response of the dependent variable to changes in the values of the independent variables

ii) Over-reactions of the dependent variable to changes in the independent variables

iii) Omission of relevant explanatory variables that are autocorrelated

iv) Outliers in the data
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question:
Which of the following are characteristics of a stationary process?

i) It crosses its mean value frequently


ii) It has constant mean and variance


iii) It contains no trend component


iv) It will be stationary in first difference form
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which of the following statements is TRUE concerning the standard regression model?
option_c: The disturbance term is assumed to be correlated with x
option_d: For an adequate model, the residual (u-hat) will be zero for all sample data points

question: If a Durbin Watson statistic takes a value close to zero, what will be the value of the first order autocorrelation coefficient?
option_d: Close to either minus one or plus one

question:

1) Lag 1 2 3

2) Coefficient 0.2 -0.15 -0.1

3) Assuming that the coefficients are approximately normally distributed, which of the coefficients are statistically significant at the 5% level?

question: Which one of the following is examined by looking at a goodness of fit statistic?
option_a: How well the population regression function fits the data
option_b: How well the sample regression function fits the population regression function
option_c: How well the sample regression function fits the data
option_d: How well the population regression function fits the sample regression function.

question: Note that statistical tables are not necessary to answer this question. For a sample of 1000 observations, the Dickey-Fuller test statistic values are
option_a: More negative than (i.e. bigger in absolute value than) those in the left hand tail of a normal distribution
option_b: Less negative than (i.e. smaller in absolute value than) those in the left hand tail of a normal distribution
option_c: Obtained from an analytical formula for the density of the Dickey-Fuller distribution
option_d: More negative (i.e. bigger in absolute value) for a 10% size of test than a 5% test.

question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the random effects approach to estimating a panel model?
option_a: The approach may not be valid if the composite error term is correlated with one or more of the explanatory variables
option_b: The number of parameters to estimate may be large, resulting in a loss of degrees of freedom
option_c: The random effects approach can only capture cross-sectional heterogeneity and not temporal variation in the dependent variable.
option_d: All of (a) to (c) are potential disadvantages of the random effects approach.

question: Which one of the following statements is true concerning VARs?
option_a: The coefficient estimates have intuitive theoretical interpretations
option_b: The coefficient estimates usually have the same sign for all of the lags of a given variable in a given equation
option_c: VARs often produce better forecasts than simultaneous equation structural models
option_d: All of the components of a VAR must be stationary before it can be used for forecasting

question:

$y_t = \beta_1 + \beta_2 x_2 + \beta_3 x_{3t} + u_t$

What is the appropriate critical value for a 2-sided 5% size of test of $H_0: \beta_3 = 1$?

A dependent variable whose values are not observable outside a certain range but where the corresponding values of the independent variables are still available would be most accurately described as what kind of variable?
option_d: Discrete choice

question: Which one of the following statements best describes a Type II error?
option_a: It is the probability of incorrectly rejecting the null hypothesis
option_b: It is equivalent to the power of the test
option_c: It is equivalent to the size of the test
option_d: It is the probability of failing to reject a null hypothesis that was wrong

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning a triangular or recursive system?

i) The parameters can be validly estimated using separate applications of OLS to

each equation


ii) The independent variables may be correlated with the error terms in other

equations


iii) An application of 2SLS would lead to unbiased but inefficient parameter estimates


iv) The independent variables may be correlated with the error terms in the equations

in which they appear as independent variables
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which one of the following statements best describes the algebraic representation of the fitted regression line?
option_d: y_t = \hat{\alpha} + \hat{\beta}x_t + \hat{u}_t

question: What is the meaning of the term "heteroscedasticity"?
option_a: The variance of the errors is not constant
option_b: The variance of the dependent variable is not constant
option_c: The errors are not linearly independent of one another
option_d: The errors have non-zero mean

question: If the standard tools for time-series analysis, such as estimation of the acf, pacf and spectral analysis, find no evidence of structure in the data, this implies that the data are which of the following?
option_d: Fat-tailed

question: Which one of the following would be a plausible response to a finding of residual non-normality?
option_a: Use a logarithmic functional form instead of a linear one
option_b: Add lags of the variables on the right hand side of the regression model
option_c: Estimate the model in first differenced form
option_d: Remove any large outliers from the data.

question:
Which of the following are plausible approaches to dealing with residual autocorrelation?

i) Take logarithms of each of the variables

ii) Add lagged values of the variables to the regression equation

iii) Use dummy variables to remove outlying observations

iv) Try a model in first differenced form rather than in levels.
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Suppose that 100 separate firms were tested to determine how many of them "beat the market" using a Jensen-type regression, and it is found that 3 fund managers significantly do so. Does this suggest prima facie evidence for stock market inefficiency?
option_c: In order to answer this question, you would need to test every fund manager trading in that market
option_d: There is insufficient information given in the question to draw a conclusion about market efficiency.

question: If a series, y, follows a random walk with drift b, what is the optimal one-step ahead forecast of the change in y?
option_d: The average value of the change in y over the in-sample period

question: For an autoregressive process to be considered stationary
option_a: The roots of the characteristic equation must all lie inside the unit circle
option_b: The roots of the characteristic equation must all lie on the unit circle
option_c: The roots of the characteristic equation must all lie outside the unit circle
option_d: The roots of the characteristic equation must all be less than one in absolute value

question:
Which of the following statements are correct concerning the use of antithetic variates as part of a Monte Carlo experiment?

i) Antithetic variates work by reducing the number of replications required to cover the whole probability space

ii) Antithetic variates involve employing a similar variable to that used in the simulation, but whose properties are known analytically

iii) Antithetic variates involve using the negative of each of the random draws and repeating the experiment using those values as the draws

iv) Antithetic variates involve taking one over each of the random draws and repeating the experiment using those values as the draws
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT concerning a comparison of the Box-Pierce Q and the Ljung-Box Q* statistics for linear dependence in time series?
option_a: Asymptotically, the values of the two test statistics will be equal
option_b: The Q test has better small-sample properties than the Q*
option_c: The Q test is sometimes over-sized for small samples
option_d: As the sample size tends towards infinity, both tests will show a tendency to always reject the null hypothesis of zero autocorrelation coefficients.

question: Including relevant lagged values of the dependent variable on the right hand side of a regression equation could lead to which one of the following?
option_d: Unbiased and consistent but inefficient coefficient estimates.

question:
Which of the following conditions are necessary for a series to be classifiable as a weakly stationary process?

(i) It must have a constant mean

(ii) It must have a constant variance

(iii) It must have constant autocovariances for given lags

(iv) It must have a constant probability distribution
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which one of the following statements is true concerning alternative forecast accuracy measures?
option_a: Mean squared error is usually highly correlated with trading rule profitability
option_b: Mean absolute error provides a quadratic loss function
option_c: Mean absolute percentage error is a useful measure for evaluating asset return forecasts
option_d: Mean squared error penalises large forecast errors disproportionately more than small forecast errors

question: The order condition is

option_b: A necessary but not sufficient condition for identification
option_c: A sufficient but not necessary condition for identification
option_d: A condition that is nether necessary nor sufficient for identification

question: If an estimator is said to have minimum variance, which of the following statements is NOT implied?
option_a: The probability that the estimate is a long way away from its true value is minimised
option_c: Such an estimator would be termed "best"
option_d: Such an estimator will always be unbiased

question: Under the null hypothesis of a Bera-Jarque test, the distribution has
option_b: Zero skewness and a kurtosis of three
option_c: Skewness of one and zero kurtosis
option_d: Skewness of one and kurtosis of three.

question:
Which of the following statements are true concerning information criteria?

(i) Adjusted R-squared is an information criterion

(ii) If the residual sum of squares falls when an additional term is added, the value of the information criterion will fall

(iii) Akaike's information criterion always leads to model orders that are at least as large as those of Schwarz's information criterion

(iv) Akaike's information criterion is consistent
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Negative residual autocorrelation is indicated by which one of the following?
option_a: A cyclical pattern in the residuals
option_b: An alternating pattern in the residuals
option_c: A complete randomness in the residuals
option_d: Residuals that are all close to zero

question:
Which of the following statements will be true if the number of replications used in a Monte Carlo study is small?

i) The statistic of interest may be estimated imprecisely


ii) The results may be affected by unrepresentative combinations of random draws


iii) The standard errors on the estimated quantities may be unacceptably large


iv) Variance reduction techniques can be used to reduce the standard errors
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question:
Which of the following are plausible approaches to dealing with a model that exhibits heteroscedasticity?

i) Take logarithms of each of the variables

ii) Use suitably modified standard errors

iii) Use a generalised least squares procedure

iv) Add lagged values of the variables to the regression equation.
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: Which one of the following is NOT a plausible remedy for near multicollinearity?
option_b: Drop one of the collinear variables
option_c: Use a longer run of data
option_d: Take logarithms of each of the variables

question: Suppose that we wished to evaluate the factors that affected the probability that an investor would choose an equity fund rather than a bond fund or a cash investment. Which class of model would be most appropriate?
option_d: An ordered logit model

question:
Which of the following may be consequences of one or more of the CLRM assumptions being violated?

i) The coefficient estimates are not optimal


ii) The standard error estimates are not optimal


iii) The distributions assumed for the test statistics are inappropriate


iv) Conclusions regarding the strength of relationships between the dependent

and independent variables may be invalid.
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: If an estimator is said to be consistent, it is implied that
option_a: On average, the estimated coefficient values will equal the true values
option_b: The OLS estimator is unbiased and no other unbiased estimator has a smaller variance
option_c: The estimates will converge upon the true values as the sample size increases
option_d: The coefficient estimates will be as close to their true values as possible for small and large samples.

question:

$y_t = -3u_{t-1} + u_{t-2} + u_t$

are

option_a: The PRF is the estimated model

question: Which of the following is a disadvantage of the fixed effects approach to estimating a panel model?
option_a: The model is likely to be technical to estimate
option_b: The approach may not be valid if the composite error term is correlated with one or more of the explanatory variables
option_c: The number of parameters to estimate may be large, resulting in a loss of degrees of freedom
option_d: The fixed effects approach can only capture cross-sectional heterogeneity and not temporal variation in the dependent variable.

question:
A white noise process will have

(i) A zero mean

(ii) A constant variance

(iii) Autocovariances that are constant

(iv) Autocovariances that are zero except at lag zero
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question:
If OLS is used in the presence of autocorrelation, which of the following will be likely consequences?

i) Coefficient estimates may be misleading


ii) Hypothesis tests could reach the wrong conclusions


iii) Forecasts made from the model could be biased


iv) Standard errors may inappropriate
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: If a Johansen "trace" test for a null hypothesis of 2 cointegrating vectors is applied to a system containing 4 variables is conducted, which eigenvalues would be used in the test?
option_d: The second largest

question: Which of the following is a typical characteristic of financial asset return time-series?
option_d: They have no trend

question:
Which of the following are disadvantages of the Dickey-Fuller / Engle-Granger approach to testing for cointegration and modelling cointegrating relationships?

i) Only one cointegrating relationship can be estimated

ii) Particularly for small samples. There is a high chance of the tests suggestingthat variables are not cointegrated when they are

iii) It is not possible to make inferences on the cointegrating regression

iv) The procedure forces the researcher to specify which is the dependent variable and which are the independent variables.
option_d: (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)

question: If a series, y, follows a random walk, what is the optimal one-step ahead forecast of y?
option_d: The average value of y over the in-sample period

question: Which one of the following is the most appropriate definition of a 99% confidence interval?
option_a: 99% of the time in repeated samples, the interval would contain the true value of the parameter
option_b: 99% of the time in repeated samples, the interval would contain the estimated value of the parameter
option_c: 99% of the time in repeated samples, the null hypothesis will be rejected
option_d: 99% of the time in repeated samples, the null hypothesis will not be rejected when it was false
